topics.definition: TCP/IP is the standard communication protocol suite used on the Internet.
The TCP/IP model has Application, Transport, Internet and Network Access layers.
IP addresses uniquely identify devices on a network. IPv4 uses 32 bits and IPv6 uses 128 bits.
tips: IPv6 provides a much larger address space.

topics.definition: Port numbers identify services running on a device.
tips: Ports work with TCP and UDP.

topics.definition: TCP provides reliable communication, while UDP provides faster communication without guaranteed delivery.
topics.example: TCP for web, UDP for streaming

topics.definition: Domain Name System (DNS) translates domain names into IP addresses.
tips: DNS acts like the Internet's phonebook.

topics.definition: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices.
Network Address Translation allows multiple devices to share one public IP address.
tips: Improves IPv4 address usage and security.

topics.definition: Use secure protocols, proper IP planning and monitor network performance.
